title: Sales enablement: positioning, competitive briefs, pitch deck, pricing, case studies, security FAQ
author: Maya Patel
summary: This consolidated sales enablement playbook provides positioning & messaging, short competitive briefs, a recommended pitch deck outline, pricing guidance, representative case studies, and a security FAQ aimed at prospects evaluating Redwood Inference for production LLM inference.
audience: Sales reps, solutions engineers, pre-sales, partner managers, and GTM content owners.
positioning_and_messaging:
Overview:
Redwood Inference is a developer-first, production-oriented LLM inference platform that optimizes for latency, cost, reliability, and deployment flexibility across hosted, dedicated, and private modes.

Value pillars (one-liners):
- Predictable performance: Consistent p50/p95 latency and throughput across deployments with transparent benchmarks.
- Cost-efficient serving: Intelligent batching, KV/prefix caching, and quantization profiles that reduce per-token cost without sacrificing quality.
- Deployment flexibility: Hosted API for fast time-to-value, Dedicated reserved pools for enterprise scale, and Private (VPC/on-prem) for regulated workloads.
- Observability & ops-first: Per-route cost/latency breakdowns, rollout controls (canary/A-B/fallback), and integrated evals for quality monitoring.

Top-level messages for different buyer personas:
- Engineers/Platform: "Ship LLM features with predictable latency and economical inference; same API for hosted, dedicated, and private deployments."
- Product/PM: "Maintain user experience SLAs with rollbackable rollouts and model versioning; reduce cost leakage via batching and caching controls."
- Security/Compliance: "Private deployments with customer-managed network/KMS, audit logs, and enterprise SLAs for regulated workloads."

Elevator pitch (30s):
"Redwood Inference gives engineering teams a production-grade runtime and orchestration layer for LLMs
delivering predictable latency, measurable unit costs, and flexible deployment models so you can ship LLM features without building and operating a complex inference stack."
competitive_briefs:
High-level competitor comparison (talking points):
- Managed LLM APIs (Simplicity-first vendors): Strengths: easy start, broad model access. Weaknesses: limited observability, higher per-token cost at scale, fewer private options. Win themes: performance transparency, cost controls, and Dedicated/Private options.
- Cloud AI endpoints (cloud provider model hosting): Strengths: integrated infra, scale. Weaknesses: vendor lock-in, inconsistent latency across regions, less LLM-specific runtime optimizations. Win themes: optimized kernels, KV caching, and cross-region fallbacks.
- Open-source self-hosted runtimes (inference infra vendors): Strengths: control and cost potential. Weaknesses: operational burden and slower feature delivery. Win themes: out-of-the-box production features (rollouts, tracing, evals), support SLAs, and turnkey Private deployment.

Competitive brief snippets (one-paragraph each):
- Vendor A (large cloud provider): "Vendor A provides managed endpoints as part of a full cloud stack. For customers who need single-cloud simplicity, they fit. We beat them on LLM-specific kernel selection, consistent p95 at tail latencies, and our Dedicated offering that isolates workload and provides predictable billing."
- Vendor B (simplicity API): "Vendor B is great for prototypes. For customers moving to production, call out our observability (per-route cost/latency), and dev experience for pinning model versions and canary rollouts."
- Vendor C (self-hosted runtime): "Vendor C appeals to teams that want full control. Emphasize Redwood’s lower operational cost of ownership: we provide optimized runtime, model onboarding, and a private deployment option backed by support and upgrades
so teams get control without hiring a dedicated ops org."
pitch_deck_outline:
Recommended pitch deck (10-12 slides):
1) Title & Hook — 1 line value prop + prospect logo (if allowed)
2) Problem — scale, latency variability, cost leakage, ops burden of serving LLMs
3) Why now — model availability, latency-sensitive UX, cost pressures
4) Redwood overview — product surface (Redwood API, Dedicated, Private, Console, Optimize)
5) How it works (high level) — runtime, kernel selection, routing, caching
6) Performance proof points — p50/p95 numbers, throughput benchmarks, cost per-1k tokens examples
7) Deployment options & pricing model — hosted vs dedicated vs private (high-level)
8) Security & compliance — VPC, KMS/HSM, audit logs, SOC/ISO (if applicable)
9) Case study — short customer story with outcome metrics (latency, cost, time-to-prod)
10) Rollout and next steps — pilot program, success criteria, timeline
11) Commercials — sample pricing, discount & procurement path
12) Appendix — integration checklist, FAQ, technical contacts

Deck notes: keep slides technical for platform buyers, but include a concise non-technical cover for executive sponsors. Use benchmarking charts from eng-serving-runtime and Console exports for latency/throughput visuals.
pricing_guidance:
Guiding principles:
- Use usage-based pricing for hosted API (per-token + per-embedding unit) as the primary price anchor.
- Offer reserved capacity for Dedicated (monthly/annual commits) with predictable throughput SLAs.
- For Private installs, combine a platform fee + support/maintenance contract.

Typical commercial constructs (examples to propose to prospects):
1) Hosted (self-serve / enterprise):
   - Base: $0.03 / 1k input tokens, $0.06 / 1k output tokens, embeddings $0.10 / 1k items (example anchor; adjust by model).
   - Volume tiers: 10% discount at > $50k/mo, 20% at > $200k/mo.
2) Dedicated:
   - Commitment: $Xk / month per reserved GPU equivalent (sample: $12k/mo per A100-equivalent pool) with included baseline throughput and overage rates.
   - Add-ons: Burst capacity, priority support, extended retention in Console.
3) Private (VPC / on-prem):
   - One-time platform fee (covers deployment automation and license), plus annual support (8-20% of platform fee) and optional engineering services for air-gapped installs.

Quoting tips for reps and AE/SE teams:
- Always qualify expected qps, seq_len distribution, and model family early. Cost calculus depends heavily on average sequence length and cache hit rates.
- Use Redwood Optimize recommendations to show potential unit-cost reductions (common wins: 15-40% from batching + quantization).
- For enterprise deals, propose a 90-day pilot with performance KPIs, then transition to committed Dedicated pricing if throughput and SLAs are validated.
case_studies:
Representative case study: Fintech analytics startup (ExampleCo) — Hosted to Dedicated migration
Summary: ExampleCo shipped a conversational analytics feature to customers and moved from hosted to Dedicated after 4 months to reduce per-session cost and stabilize latency.
Key outcomes:
- Latency: p95 down from 1.2s to 420ms for 512-token requests after kernel tuning and batching.
- Cost: estimated per-session inference cost reduced by 38% after enabling KV caching and a 4-bit quantization profile for a compatible model.
- Time-to-prod: integration completed in 10 days using Redwood API and Console rollouts.
Implementation notes:
1) Baseline benchmark run (SE-led) to capture seq_len distribution and tail latencies.
2) Enable KV / prefix caching for conversational flows; tune cache TTL to session lengths.
3) Migrate to Dedicated reserved pool with autoscaling policy set to 2x baseline sustained qps.

Representative enterprise case study: Regulated healthcare customer (HealthCo) — Private deployment
Summary: HealthCo required data residency and auditability. Redwood delivered a Private (VPC) deployment with customer-managed KMS and monthly compliance reviews.
Key outcomes:
- Compliance: integrated audit logging and SIEM forwarding within 30 days.
- Support: 24/7 enterprise support and a quarterly security review cadence.
- Business impact: launched a triage assistant product internally within 6 weeks and began pilot with patients in controlled study.

Include short one-pagers for each case study that quantify latency, cost, time-to-prod, and key contacts for references.
security_faq:
Security FAQ for prospects (short answers for initial evaluation):
Q: What deployment options support data residency and network isolation?
A: Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments support full network isolation; Dedicated provides tenancy isolation and strict networking controls.

Q: How is customer data protected at rest and in transit?
A: Data in transit uses TLS1.2+; at-rest encryption via customer-managed KMS is available for Private deployments and for Dedicated on request.

Q: Do you support customer-managed keys / HSM?
A: Yes — Private deployments support KMS/HSM integration; for Dedicated we support KMS integration with contractual terms.

Q: What audit and logging capabilities are available?
A: Redwood Console provides request-level telemetry, audit logs, and integrations with common SIEMs. For Private deployments, logs can be forwarded to customer logging pipelines.

Q: How do you handle model and prompt data retention?
A: Retention policies are configurable per-customer. We recommend minimal retention (30 days) for logs used in diagnostics and offer a compliance package for longer retention and export controls.

Q: Certifications / compliance?
A: Redwood maintains SOC2 readiness artifacts and common compliance evidence; for regulated customers we provide a compliance review checklist and enable Private deployment controls to meet contractual obligations.

Q: Incident response and breach notification?
A: We publish an incident-response process and commit to contractual notification SLAs for enterprise customers. For Private deployments we can integrate with a customer playbook and run joint incident drills.

Q: Where do models run?
A: Models run on customer-chosen compute for Private, on dedicated pools for Dedicated, and on Redwood-managed infrastructure for Hosted with transparent region selection.

Notes for SEs: capture security contact early. Route detailed compliance requests to security-and-compliance team; use the related_pages links for evidence artifacts.
sales_talk_tracks:
Lead-in scripts and objection handlers:
Cold intro (30s): 
"Many teams start with prototypes that work fine, but when traffic increases the cost and latency variability become blockers. Redwood gives you a single runtime with predictable latency, cost controls, and private deployment options so you can move from prototype to production without building inference infra."

Technical deep-dive opener (for SRE/Platform):
"We focus on inference economics: kernel selection, continuous batching, and KV caching that can reduce per-token cost by up to ~40% while preserving p95 tail SLOs. Tell me about your sequence lengths and peak qps so I can map expected savings."

Common objections and responses:
- "We can self-host and save money." -> "Self-hosting can save raw infra costs, but don't underestimate MTTD/MTTR, model onboarding, and ongoing ops costs. We offer Private deployments plus managed services to remove that burden."
- "How do we avoid vendor lock-in?" -> "We support model portability, version pinning, and can run in your VPC/on-prem—so you retain control while getting our runtime optimizations."

next_steps:
Suggested next steps for reps:
1) Run quick qualifying questionnaire (qps, average sequence length, model types, security requirements).
2) Propose a 30-90 day pilot with defined KPIs (p95 latency target, cost per 1k tokens target, stability metrics).
3) Coordinate SE+Security scoping call and deliver a pilot statement of work (use templates).
4) If success criteria met, transition to Dedicated commitment or Private deployment proposal using the Dedicated quoting worksheet.
